title: Can I Return It Without the Receipt?
prerequisites: understand can or could for permission
observable_outcome: The learner asks whether alternative proof is accepted and accurately restates the return deadline and item condition.
learning_objective: Ask whether a shop can accept a return without a receipt, then confirm the deadline and required item condition.

scenario.setting: A fictional clothing shop return counter.
scenario.prompt: You bought a sweater 12 days ago. It is unused and the tag is attached. You lost the paper receipt, but your bank statement shows the purchase. The shop policy accepts returns within 30 days with proof of purchase.
scenario.puzzle: What can replace the receipt as proof, and which deadline and condition must you confirm?
scenario.privacy_note: The shop, purchase, policy, employee, and customer are fictional teaching data. The activity is language practice, not legal advice.

model.clarify: Could I return this without the paper receipt? I have the bank statement.
model.customer_reply: The sweater is unused, and the tag is still attached.
model.confirm: So I can return it within 30 days with proof of purchase, and it must be unused with the tag attached, right?
model.neutral_variant: Can I use my bank statement as proof of purchase instead of the receipt?

language_focus.grammar: Can I ...? asks for permission. Could I ...? is more formal and polite. Without names something that is absent. Instead of presents an alternative: a bank statement instead of the receipt.
language_focus.meaning: The question checks whether alternative proof is accepted. The readback separates three policy details: proof of purchase, the 30-day deadline, and the required condition of the item.
language_focus.appropriateness: Could I ...? suits a polite service encounter. Explaining what proof you do have is more useful than only saying what is missing. Confirming the deadline and condition prevents another misunderstanding.
language_focus.detail_language: Within 30 days means no later than the end of that period. With the tag attached describes the item's required condition. This lesson uses a fictional shop policy; real rights and policies vary by place and purchase type.

choice_activity.prompt: Which evidence best replaces the missing paper receipt in this scenario?

options.text: The bank statement showing the purchase
options.feedback: Correct. The scenario says the statement shows the purchase and the shop accepts proof of purchase.
A bag may come from the shop, but it does not clearly show this purchase. Use the bank statement.
The fictional policy asks for proof of purchase. Offer the bank statement rather than no evidence.

request_activity.prompt: Which question clearly checks permission and offers the alternative proof?

options.text: Could I return this without the paper receipt? I have the bank statement.
options.feedback: Correct. It politely asks permission and immediately names the available proof.

options.text: Can I use my bank statement as proof of purchase instead of the receipt?
options.feedback: Also correct. It directly checks whether the alternative evidence is acceptable.

options.text: I lost it. Give me a refund.
options.feedback: This does not identify the available proof or check the policy. Ask whether the bank statement is accepted.

slot_activity.prompt: Match each policy detail to its slot.

feedback.proof: Correct. It shows evidence of the purchase in this scenario.
feedback.item condition: Unused with the tag attached describes the condition.

feedback.proof: The bank statement is the proof.
feedback.deadline: Correct. This is the time limit for the fictional policy.
feedback.item condition: The item's condition is unused with the tag attached.

feedback.proof: The proof is the bank statement.
feedback.item condition: Correct. These words describe how the sweater must be returned.

production_task.scenario: You bought headphones online 20 days ago. They are unopened. You have the purchase email but no paper receipt. The fictional policy allows returns within 28 days with proof of purchase.
production_task.instruction: Write one polite question about the purchase email. Then confirm the 28-day deadline and unopened condition.
acceptable_responses: Could I use the purchase email as proof instead of a paper receipt? So I can return the headphones within 28 days if they are unopened, right?
Can I return these without a paper receipt? I have the purchase email. The deadline is 28 days and the box must be unopened, correct?
rubric: I confirmed the required item condition.
production_task.valid_variants: Can I ...? and Could I ...? are both possible; could is more formal and polite. Right?, correct?, and Is that right? can all invite confirmation.

review_prompt: Tomorrow, recall the three return-policy slots: proof, deadline, and item condition. Make one confirmation question using all three.

visual.title: Proof, deadline, condition

sources.inspected: The official guidance says a business may ask for proof of purchase and that evidence can include a sales receipt, bank statement, or packaging.
